_comment: The libgit2 port campaign's out-of-tree libraries, in the schema of Crustify 043a8ae, as planner run 11 brought them to it from run 10's assessments: each library's candidate crates, each with one quality_assessment composed from run 10's reading of it against the Adopted crates criteria (coverage, shared state, soundness, advisories, maintenance) and its verdict; every entity the campaign uses of the library (c_entities), from the external records of schedule.json's modules, named by the public header that declares it, with the modules that use it, what each candidate and std offers for it and the plan's recommended route, by the area run 10 assessed it in; and the recommendation that follows. Each library's decision is the user's, as recorded after run 11 (fb010a58e): the crates it adopts, the route of what they leave uncovered, and the overrides of the entities whose recommended route it does not take. libz-rs-sys, assessed by run 10, is no candidate: it has no safe API. Planner run 12 took each entity's used_by from its schedule, whose macros reference out-of-tree entities too (wavefront e529c26). Planner run 11's composition is crustify/artifacts/planner/run-11/compose/ (deps11.py), run 12's crustify/artifacts/planner/run-12/compose/ (deps12.py).

candidates.quality_assessment: Not fit: coverage. It has no mktime: no normalisation of out-of-range fields and no tm_isdst hint, so the clocks and calendar time area it was assessed for stays with the crustify campaign. Coverage: Calendar conversion only: Utc/Local from a timestamp (gmtime_r, localtime_r), reading TZ and /etc/localtime with its own tzfile parser. It has no mktime equivalent: it does not normalise out-of-range tm fields (date.c:564 relies on that) and takes no tm_isdst hint (signature.c:172 relies on mktime reading a gmtime result with tm_isdst=0 as standard time). Local::from_local_datetime returns ambiguous or none instead. clock_gettime, gettimeofday, time and difftime are std's (Instant, SystemTime). Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): 10 unsafe blocks, no public unsafe fn. On Linux they are a NonZeroI32::new_unchecked on a checked value (naive/date/mod.rs:1496), from_utf8_unchecked over validated tz names (offset/local/tz_info/timezone.rs:550) and CStr::from_bytes_with_nul_unchecked after locating the NUL (offset/local/tz_data.rs:158). Since 0.4.20 it no longer calls libc localtime_r (lib.rs:457-472). No RustSec advisory affects 0.4.45. Maintenance: last released 2026-06-04, published by the chronotope organization (github:chronotope:release-manager) and lifthrasiir; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Fit for files, directories and file metadata; sockets, name resolution and polling; process identity, users and system information; and errno and error strings. Coverage: Calls glibc itself, so behaviour and errno side effects are glibc's. Covers files: open/fcntl (O_FSYNC on Linux gnu), stat/lstat/fstat with FileStat = libc::stat, fchmodat, mkdir, utimes, futimens, readlink, access, linkat/symlinkat/renameat/unlinkat (for rmdir), fsync, lseek, read/write, pread/pwrite, getcwd and Dir. Covers sockets: socket, connect, send, recv, sockopt KeepAlive/TcpKeepIdle/TcpKeepInterval/TcpKeepCount/SocketError, and poll. Also covers the get*id calls, sysconf, User::from_uid (getpwuid_r), sysinfo load_average, Errno last/set, pthread_sigmask, SigSet and SigSet::wait (sigwait), execve, pipe, dup2, chdir and waitpid. Lacks realpath, getaddrinfo/gai_strerror and inet_pton (std covers these), sigpending and getentropy. fork, signal, sigaction, mmap and munmap are unsafe fns. Errno::desc is nix's own table, so strerror text differs (EAGAIN gives 'Try again'; glibc gives 'Resource temporarily unavailable'). getloadavg goes through sysinfo(2) loads at 1/65536 precision. No stdio, string, ctype, qsort, calendar conversion, pthread mutex/rwlock/cond/key or malloc. Shared state: It exposes the state it holds to C (raw descriptors or handles). Soundness (sound): 749 unsafe blocks and 59 pub unsafe fns; the operations unsafe by nature are unsafe fns (unistd.rs:278 fork, sys/signal.rs:930 sigaction, :992 signal, sys/mman.rs:427 mmap, :540 munmap). fds are std OwnedFd/BorrowedFd/AsFd, and PollFd<'fd> carries the borrow (poll.rs:18-20). Dir owns a NonNull<DIR> and is Send but not Sync (dir.rs:47,124). Growing buffers pass their capacity and set_len to the returned length (unistd.rs:937-950 getcwd, fcntl.rs:554-631 readlink, unistd.rs:3714-3745 getpwuid_r). Not UB: from_anything tests Errno::last()==ERANGE rather than getpwuid_r's return value (unistd.rs:3740). No RustSec advisory affects 0.31.3. Maintenance: last released 2026-05-11, published by the nix-rust organization's nix-maintainers team and one maintainer (carllerche); license MIT.

candidates.license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
candidates.quality_assessment: Not fit: maintenance. One crates.io owner publishes it; it otherwise covers files and sockets. Coverage: Covers files: open, stat/lstat/fstat, chmod, mkdir, rmdir, unlink, link, symlink, readlink, rename, access, utimensat/futimens, fsync, seek, read/write/pread/pwrite, fcntl_getfl/setfl/getfd/setfd, getcwd, chdir and Dir. Covers sockets: socket_with, connect, send, recv, keepalive/keepidle/keepintvl/keepcnt, socket_error and poll. Also covers the get*id calls, page_size, getrandom, clock_gettime, sysinfo loads, pipe, dup2 and waitpid. Lacks realpath, getaddrinfo, inet_pton, getpwuid_r, sysconf (_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN, _SC_GETPW_R_SIZE_MAX) and an errno setter. fork, execve and signal masks exist only in its unsafe, semver-exempt runtime feature; mmap and munmap are unsafe fns. Its default Linux backend makes raw syscalls and leaves errno untouched, so a ported function whose C callers read errno must set errno some other way (the libc backend, --cfg rustix_use_libc, leaves glibc's errno). It fails the maintenance criterion alone: one crates.io owner publishes it. Shared state: It exposes the state it holds to C (raw descriptors or handles). Soundness (sound): 1067 unsafe blocks and 70 pub unsafe fns, mostly mm/mmap.rs (9), the runtime module (16) and io_uring; none in the file, socket or id calls used. Every call takes AsFd/BorrowedFd, output buffers go through the sealed Buffer trait (buffer.rs:106-165), and Dir owns an OwnedFd (backend/linux_raw/fs/dir.rs:17-19). The xattr zero-length-buffer UB (RUSTSEC-2026-0486) is fixed in 1.1.6 and outside the used surface. No RustSec advisory affects 1.1.6. Maintenance: last released 2026-10-27, published by one crates.io owner (sunfishcode), from the bytecodealliance organization's repository; license Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT.

Fit for sockets, name resolution and polling; nix is recommended there, as it covers the other areas too. Coverage: Sockets only. Socket::new sets SOCK_CLOEXEC (socket.rs:744-), connect_timeout does a non-blocking connect, poll and SO_ERROR as socket.c does (socket.rs:215, sys/unix.rs:973), and it has set_tcp_keepalive(TcpKeepalive with_time/with_interval/with_retries), take_error, send/recv and set_nonblocking. Lacks getaddrinfo/gai_strerror and inet_pton (std::net covers them) and a general poll: its send/recv timeouts are SO_SNDTIMEO/SO_RCVTIMEO, where socket.c polls on EAGAIN. Shared state: It exposes the state it holds to C (raw descriptors or handles). Soundness (sound): 215 unsafe blocks and 3 pub unsafe fns (sockaddr.rs:73 view_as, :197 try_init, :232 set_length). Socket wraps an OwnedFd (sys/unix.rs:940); raw fds enter only through unsafe FromRawFd (sys/unix.rs:3057) or the crate-private from_raw fed by syscalls (socket.rs:86). The sockaddr layout cast of RUSTSEC-2020-0079 is fixed since 0.3.16. No RustSec advisory affects 0.6.5. Maintenance: last released 2026-07-13, published by the rust-lang organization (repo rust-lang/socket2; owners sfackler, Thomasdezeeuw, rust-lang-owner, github:tokio-rs:socket2); license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Not fit: coverage and shared state. Its file-backed constructors are unsafe fns and it cannot adopt a mapping C created. Coverage: Memory maps only: Mmap and MmapMut over a file (MAP_SHARED with write through map_mut, MAP_PRIVATE through map_copy). Every file-backed constructor is an unsafe fn (lib.rs:557, 633, 677, 933, 1453). The only safe ones are map_if_safe, for sealed memfds or fs-verity files only (lib.rs:757), and MmapRaw, which yields a raw pointer. It cannot adopt or release a mapping given as (data, len), so a git_map created or unmapped by C cannot be shared. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): 72 unsafe blocks and 17 pub unsafe fns. Its safe Deref gives a slice over the mapping it owns (lib.rs:1103, 1698, 1705), with Send/Sync on MmapInner (unix.rs:658-659). The constructors' contract, that the file is not modified or truncated, is left to the caller. The out-of-range advise/flush offsets of RUSTSEC-2026-0186 are fixed in 0.9.11. No RustSec advisory affects 0.9.12. Maintenance: last released 2026-10-21, published by four maintainers (tbu-, RazrFalcon, de-vri-es, allan2); license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

candidates.quality_assessment: Fit for the SHA-256 digest. Coverage: covers only the SHA-256 area: Sha256::new/update/finalize replace SHA256_Init/Update/Final with identical output. It is not a C-layout SHA256_CTX: git_hash_sha256_ctx is embedded by value in git_hash_ctx (src/util/hash.h:28-34), which sits inside git_filebuf (src/util/filebuf.h:40) and pack-objects.h:65, so the hash port keeps that layout until its port/layout. Only src/util/hash/openssl.c touches the state. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): 39 unsafe lines, all SIMD/asm compress backends selected after cpufeatures detection (src/sha256.rs:56-72); x86_sha.rs:48-70 makes unaligned loads within [u8;64]/[u32;8]; soft/unroll.rs:39 reads K32[i] with i<64; block-buffer 0.12.1 (22 unsafe) checks its position invariant before each unchecked set (lib.rs:239-245). No RustSec advisory affects 0.11.1. Maintenance: last released 2026-10-12, published by the RustCrypto organization; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Fit for the NTLM digests, with md-5 and md4. Coverage: HMAC_CTX_new/reset/free/Init_ex/Update/Final become Hmac<Md5>::new_from_slice (any key length), update and finalize; a re-init is a new value. The digest comes from md-5, so hmac covers its area only with md-5 and md4. The HMAC_CTX* lives in ntlm_client.crypt_ctx (deps/ntlmclient/ntlm.h:72), but only crypt_openssl.c touches it. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): no unsafe in hmac/src; its digest 0.11.3 dependency forbids unsafe_code. No RustSec advisory affects 0.13.0. Maintenance: last released 2026-03-29, published by the RustCrypto organization; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Fit for the NTLM digests, as hmac's MD5. Coverage: MD5 only, in EVP_md5's role as hmac's digest parameter. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): its only unsafe, src/compress/loongarch64_asm.rs:70 (inline asm), is not compiled on x86_64. No RustSec advisory affects 0.11.0. Maintenance: last released 2026-03-27, published by the RustCrypto organization; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Fit for the NTLM digests (MD4). Coverage: MD4 only: the one-shot MD4() becomes Md4::digest. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in src/lib.rs. No RustSec advisory affects 0.11.0. Maintenance: last released 2026-03-27, published by the RustCrypto organization; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Fit for DES-ECB. Coverage: DES_set_key/DES_ecb_encrypt become Des::new and encrypt_block. Like OpenSSL 3.0.13's DES_set_key, which schedules any key whatever its parity or weakness (crypto/des/set_key.c:298-306) and whose result ntlmclient ignores, it ignores parity bits and accepts weak keys (src/des.rs:46-51). Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): des and cipher 0.5.0 forbid unsafe_code; inout 0.2.6 (31 unsafe lines) builds in/out views only from &mut or (&, &mut) pairs of checked equal length (inout_buf.rs:72-80), and its from_raw is unsafe. No RustSec advisory affects 0.9.0. Maintenance: last released 2026-04-10, published by the RustCrypto organization; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Fit for random bytes. Coverage: RAND_bytes becomes getrandom::fill: the bytes come from the kernel's CSPRNG rather than OpenSSL's DRBG, and a failure is a getrandom::Error rather than ERR_lib_error_string's text. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): its safe API is fill(&mut [u8]) and fill_uninit(&mut [MaybeUninit<u8>]) (src/lib.rs:87-130); the Linux backend calls libc::getrandom on the exact buffer (backends/getrandom.rs); 114 unsafe lines across the platform backends. No RustSec advisory affects 0.4.3. Maintenance: last released 2026-06-17, published by the rust-random organization; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Not fit: coverage. No subject CN for the CN fallback and no ASN.1 string API. Coverage: verifies chains and SAN DNS and IP names only: no subject CN for libgit2's CN fallback, no ASN1 string API, and the C caller's X509* (GIT_OPT_ADD_SSL_X509_CERT) only as DER, through i2d_X509; its verification rules differ from X509_verify_cert's. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): no unsafe in src; no_std. No RustSec advisory affects 0.103.16. Maintenance: last released 2026-10-20, published by the rustls organization; license ISC.

Not fit: soundness. A small fork fixing bread and X509StoreRef::objects would make it qualify for libssl and for libcrypto's X.509 and BIO areas. Coverage: Covers X509 (subject_alt_names with dnsname/ipaddress, subject_name().entries_by_nid, X509NameEntryRef::data, to_der), Asn1StringRef::to_string, openssl::sha::Sha256 over SHA256_CTX, PKey::hmac with Signer and MessageDigest::md5, rand_bytes and ErrorStack. MD4 (Md::fetch) and DES-ECB (Cipher::des_ecb) go through EVP, so OpenSSL 3 needs its legacy provider loaded, where the low-level MD4()/DES_* do not. No BIO_meth_* API (SslStream<S: Read + Write> builds its own BIO method), no ASN1_STRING_type accessor, and CRYPTO_malloc/free stay internal; its error Display adds file:line to ERR_error_string_n's format. Soundness (unsound): ssl/bio.rs:107-113: bread makes a &mut [u8] over OpenSSL's read buffer, which OPENSSL_malloc allocates and never zeroes (ssl/record/ssl3_buffer.c:68), and hands it to the user's safe S::read; x509/store.rs:261-273: X509StoreRef::objects is a safe pub fn the crate documents as unsound (deprecated). 1245 unsafe lines; the paths the campaign would use were read. No RustSec advisory affects 0.10.82. Maintenance: last released 2026-11-01, published by two maintainers (sfackler, alex), in the rust-openssl organization's repository; license Apache-2.0.

candidates.quality_assessment: Not fit: coverage. No cipher lists, no verify-none-then-report flow, no CN fallback. Coverage: ClientConfig/ClientConnection over any Read + Write replace SSL_CTX, SSL and the custom BIO, with SNI, peer_certificates (DER) and TLS 1.2 and later only, which matches libgit2's SSL_OP_NO_* set. Gaps: no OpenSSL cipher-list strings, so GIT_OPT_SET_SSL_CIPHERS cannot be honoured; libgit2 completes the handshake with SSL_VERIFY_NONE, reads SSL_get_verify_result and returns GIT_ECERTIFICATE so that the user's certificate_check callback may override it (src/libgit2/transports/httpclient.c:837), which needs a custom danger::ServerCertVerifier, and verification is webpki's, not OpenSSL's; no CN fallback; verify paths need rustls-native-certs, which loads eagerly rather than through OpenSSL's hashed-directory lookup; the C caller's X509* only as DER; and it needs a crypto provider, aws-lc-rs by default, which bundles AWS-LC. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (src/lib.rs:332); rustls-webpki and rustls-native-certs have no unsafe; the default aws-lc-rs provider (381 unsafe lines over the bundled AWS-LC) was not read. No RustSec advisory affects 0.23.46. Maintenance: last released 2026-10-14, published by the rustls organization; license Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT.

Not fit: soundness. A small fork fixing bread and X509StoreRef::objects would make it qualify for libssl and for libcrypto's X.509 and BIO areas. Coverage: SslContextBuilder covers SSL_CTX_new(TLS_method), set_options (NO_SSLV2/3, NO_TLSV1/1_1, NO_COMPRESSION), set_mode(AUTO_RETRY), set_verify(NONE), set_default_verify_paths, set_cipher_list, load_verify_locations and cert_store_mut().add_cert; Ssl::new, set_hostname (SNI), SslStream's connect, ssl_read, ssl_write and shutdown, ssl::Error::code (SSL_get_error), peer_certificate and verify_result cover the connection. A built SslContext is immutable, while libgit2 changes the live git__ssl_ctx through git_openssl__set_cert_location and git_openssl__add_x509_cert, so a port rebuilds the context on each such option; SSL_set_bio over libgit2's BIO becomes SslStream<S> over a Read + Write adapter of git_stream; OPENSSL_init_ssl is implicit. Shared state: It exposes the state it holds to C (raw descriptors or handles). Soundness (unsound): SslStream<S> reaches bread (ssl/bio.rs:107-113), which hands OpenSSL's unzeroed record buffer (ssl/record/ssl3_buffer.c:68) to the safe S::read as &mut [u8]; X509StoreRef::objects (x509/store.rs:261-273) is a safe API the crate documents as unsound. No RustSec advisory affects 0.10.82. Maintenance: last released 2026-11-01, published by two maintainers (sfackler, alex), in the rust-openssl organization's repository; license Apache-2.0.

Not fit: soundness, through openssl's SslStream, and coverage. Coverage: A platform facade over the openssl crate on Linux: no cipher list, no verify-locations directory, no SSL_VERIFY_NONE-then-report flow (an invalid certificate fails the handshake unless danger_accept_invalid_certs), no verify result codes and no raw handles; add_root_certificate takes DER only. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (unsound): its Linux TlsStream<S> is openssl::ssl::SslStream<S> (src/imp/openssl.rs:431), so it inherits bread's &mut [u8] over uninitialised memory (openssl ssl/bio.rs:107-113); its own 2 unsafe lines are macOS-only. No RustSec advisory affects 0.2.18. Maintenance: last released 2026-02-18, published by two maintainers (sfackler, kornelski); license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

candidates.quality_assessment: Not fit: coverage. Not PCRE2's dialect. Coverage: Not PCRE2's syntax or semantics, though it adds backreferences, lookaround, atomic and possessive groups, conditionals, subroutine calls, \K and \Z over regex-automata, and matches &[u8] through BytesMode::Ascii since 0.20. `$` matches only at the end of the text (parse.rs:375-382), where PCRE2's also matches before a final newline; patterns are Strings, so raw non-UTF-8 pattern bytes (the built-in word patterns of userdiff.h:25,160) must be rewritten as escapes; no PCRE2 verbs or options; its backtrack limit is 1e6 against PCRE2's 1e7 match limit; its error texts differ from pcre2_get_error_message's. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): no unsafe in the crate's source; its regex-automata dependency's unsafe was not read. No RustSec advisory affects 0.20.1. Maintenance: last released 2026-11-09, published by the fancy-regex organization and three maintainers; license MIT.

Not fit: coverage. Not PCRE2's dialect. Coverage: Another dialect: regex::bytes with unicode(false) and case_insensitive matches bytes with ASCII case folding, as PCRE2 does in non-UTF CASELESS mode, and CaptureLocations covers the ovector and unset groups, but it has no backreferences, lookaround, atomic or possessive groups, \Q..\E, \Z, recursion or verbs; `$` matches only at the end of the text; size limits replace PCRE2's match limits; patterns are &str; its error texts differ. Config regexes, diff drivers' xfuncname and wordregex, and revparse's :/ expose PCRE2's syntax to users. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): one unsafe site in the crate, src/pattern.rs:30 (a nightly-only Pattern impl); the engine's unsafe, in regex-automata, memchr and aho-corasick, was not read. candidates.quality_assessment: Fit for zlib streams and CRC-32. Coverage: Assessed with its default rust_backend, miniz_oxide; its zlib and zlib-ng features make it a binding over libz-sys with the same API, and zlib-rs is another backend. Compress and Decompress cover deflateInit/deflate/deflateReset/deflateEnd and their inflate counterparts (Status Ok/BufError/StreamEnd, total_in/out, reset, message()), and Crc covers crc32. No deflateBound: reftable's block.c:174-198 uses it only to size one buffer for a single Z_FINISH call, which a compress_vec loop until StreamEnd replaces. With the miniz backend a first inflate call with Finish whose output does not fit fails the stream (miniz_oxide inflate/stream.rs:227-250), where zstream.c:106-123 passes Z_FINISH with chunked output, so the port passes FlushDecompress::None (the zlib-rs backend keeps zlib's semantics); Compression::new does not reject levels above 9, which filebuf.c:317-324 turns into an error; an allocation failure aborts rather than returning Z_MEM_ERROR; the miniz backend gives no zlib message text; its output is not byte-identical to zlib 1.3's, which the formats do not require (object ids hash uncompressed data, a pack's name hashes whatever bytes it holds), though tests/libgit2/pack/indexer.c:178 asserts the name of a thin pack libgit2 deflates (unverified across compressors). Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): 37 unsafe lines, 25 of them in ffi/c.rs, compiled for its C backends only; mem.rs:647-656 clamps set_len to the capacity; ffi/mod.rs:9-11 zero-fills uninitialised output before miniz_oxide sees it; no z_stream is exposed; miniz_oxide forbids unsafe_code. No RustSec advisory affects 1.1.11. Maintenance: last released 2026-11-06, published by the rust-lang organization; license MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Not fit: soundness unclear. Its unsafe beyond the stable API was not read and no scan was run. Coverage: Its safe API covers every use: Deflate/Inflate (new, compress/decompress with NoFlush/Finish, reset, total_in/out, zlib's error_message texts), compress_bound in deflateBound's place and crc32::crc32(start, buf). Deflate::new panics on a bad level or a failed allocation rather than returning Z_STREAM_ERROR/Z_MEM_ERROR (deflate.rs:136-137); its output is not byte-identical to zlib 1.3's. Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (unclear): stable.rs sets next_in/next_out from slices, clamps avail to c_uint::MAX and clears the pointers after each call (stable.rs:357-376), and reads msg only as a static C string (stable.rs:92,290); its other ~456 unsafe lines (SIMD, allocator, C API) were not read, and no scan was run. No RustSec advisory affects 0.6.8. Maintenance: last released 2026-09-15, published by the Trifecta Tech Foundation, two maintainers; license Zlib.

Shared state: It keeps its state in Rust: nothing it holds crosses to C. Soundness (sound): #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (src/lib.rs:25). No RustSec advisory affects 0.9.1. Maintenance: last released 2026-03-13, published by two maintainers (oyvindln, Frommi); license MIT OR Zlib OR Apache-2.0.
